You are a senior frontend developer and UI/UX designer.

Build a clean, modern, FUN habit tracker app frontend.
Focus only on FRONTEND.
No AI features.
No login/signup.
No demo-looking UI.
No placeholder-heavy design.

APP TYPE:
• Mobile-first web app (PWA style)
• Simple, smooth, and realistic
• Feels like a real production app

CORE FEATURES (FRONTEND ONLY):

1️⃣ HOME / TODAY SCREEN
• App name at top
• Today’s date
• List of today’s habits
• Each habit card contains:
  - Emoji icon
  - Habit name
  - Small description
  - Circular progress / checkbox
• One-tap mark as completed
• Completed habit shows:
  - Smooth animation
  - Color change
  - Strike-through text

2️⃣ ADD HABIT SCREEN
• Add habit form with:
  - Habit name
  - Short description
  - Emoji picker (simple emoji list)
  - Color selector
  - Frequency:
    - Daily
    - Weekly
    - Custom days
• Save button
• Cancel button

3️⃣ HABIT DETAILS SCREEN
• Habit title + emoji
• Selected color theme
• Completion history (last 7 days)
• Streak count
• Edit habit button
• Delete habit button

4️⃣ STREAKS & PROGRESS SCREEN
• Total habits
• Completed today
• Current streak
• Best streak
• Weekly progress bar
• Simple bar or line chart (frontend only)

5️⃣ SETTINGS SCREEN
• Dark / Light mode toggle
• Sound on/off
• Animation on/off
• Reset all habits button

6️⃣ NAVIGATION
• Bottom navigation bar:
  - Today
  - Add Habit
  - Progress
  - Settings
• Smooth page transitions

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
• Modern card-based UI
• Rounded corners
• Soft shadows
• Pleasant colors (no neon)
• Minimal text
• Good spacing
• High-quality font (Poppins / Inter style)

INTERACTIONS:
• Smooth hover / tap effects
• Subtle animations (scale, fade)
• No heavy animation
• Fast performance

TECH REQUIREMENTS:
• HTML + CSS + JavaScript (or React)
• LocalStorage for data saving
• Clean folder structure
• Mobile responsive
• No backend
• No authentication
• No AI
• Comment code properly
• Explain how data is stored locally

OUTPUT REQUIRED:
• Fully working frontend habit tracker
• Realistic UI (not demo-looking)
• Clean code
• Easy to extend later

**Focusing on Requirements**

I'm currently zeroing in on the project's core requirements. As a senior front-end developer and UI/UX designer, my goal is to create a delightful, mobile-first PWA habit tracker. I'm carefully analyzing the limitations and scope to ensure a well-defined project foundation, especially the fun factor.


**Defining the UI/UX**

Okay, I've got a clearer vision for the UI/UX now. I'm prioritizing a mobile-first approach, with React 18+, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. I'm focusing on crafting a very user-friendly habit tracker, ensuring all the key features are incorporated, like progress charts and streaks. I'm also looking at the best way to handle habit data, and will use LocalStorage for data persistence. I'm leaning toward a `HabitContext` for state management.


**Outlining Design Preferences**

I'm now nailing down the UI design strategy. Mobile-first design is key, with a fixed bottom navigation and safe area padding. Aesthetics will be "fun" yet clean with rounded corners, soft shadows, and pastel colors. I'll use Tailwind's `transition` and `transform` utilities alongside standard React state for simple animations. For page transitions, I'll rely on CSS transitions. I'm choosing Inter via CDNs.


**Detailing Component Structures**

I'm solidifying the component breakdown for the habit tracker. I've mapped out the key files like `Layout.tsx`, `BottomNav.tsx`, and specific views for Today, Add, Detail, Progress, and Settings. I'm focusing on a clean structure, with a central `HabitContext` for all the logic.

**Implementing The Build**

I'm now outlining the implementation phase step by step. I'm starting with core files such as `metadata.json`, `index.html` (to load Tailwind and fonts), `index.tsx` (entry point), `types.ts` (interfaces), and `constants.ts` (colors, emojis, and initial data).


**Organizing Component Logic**

I'm now laying out the detailed structure of several key components. I'm focusing on `HabitContext.tsx` to handle LocalStorage and CRUD operations. I will also be building out the `Icon.tsx` wrapper for Lucide icons, the `BottomNav.tsx` tab bar, and views for Today, Add, Progress, Settings, and habit details. Finally, I'll be creating the `App.tsx` file to glue everything together. The routing will be handled via a simple View Manager state within `App.tsx`.


**Refining Habit Logic**

My focus is now on refining the habit completion and streak calculation logic. I'm strategizing how to filter habits for the Today view based on frequency, and how to effectively track completion dates. The streak calculations will check consecutive days from today, and I'll use `clsx` for conditional styling. I'm also considering a completion animation.


**Confirming Key Adjustments**

I've tested simple CSS scale animations, preferring them to external libraries. I've also confirmed that the "Add" button should be a central tab. I'm double-checking the tech stack: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind, LocalStorage, and a fully responsive design, with no separate CSS files. I've corrected the file structure, integrating logic into manageable groups, with separation of views and components. I will create `utils.ts` for date formatting and streak calculations; key is using `format(new Date(), 'yyyy-MM-dd')` for storage.

\n\n
**Defining XML Construction**

I'm now outlining XML file construction. Metadata will include the name "HabitFlow." The HTML file will include the Inter font and Tailwind script, while the types will clearly define a "Habit" interface. I will include date helpers within the utility functions.


**Analyzing Module Structures**

I'm now focusing on organizing the modules of the application. I've broken down the app into its core components: Context for state management, atomic UI elements, distinct views for each screen, and finally, the App component handling routing and layout.

\n\n
**Focusing on Fun Elements**

I'm now working to bring more "fun" into the application. I'll be using emojis, providing encouraging messages for empty states, and implementing a nice gradient for the progress bars. I'm importing Recharts to create the Progress Screen. I'll include icons via Lucide-React and use standard `date-fns` for all date formatting and manipulation.


**Finalizing Data Implementation**

I'm now fully committed to using native JavaScript Date objects, and ensuring portable data handling. My plan is to use `getTodayString()` and `getDayName()` utility functions for all date operations. I'm prioritizing minimal dependencies and broader compatibility with this strategy.
